valuesRule.note: All Australian values questions must be answered correctly, in addition to an overall mark of at least 15/20 (75%).

questions.question: On Anzac Day, we remember
options: all Australians who have fought and died in wars.
the creation of an independent Australian nation.
the arrival of the First Fleet from Great Britain.
answers: all Australians who have fought and died in wars.

questions.question: What are the colours of the Australian Aboriginal Flag?
options: Black, red and yellow.
Green, white and black.
Blue, white and green.

questions.question: What is Australia's capital city?
options: Canberra.
Brisbane.
Perth.

questions.question: When did the separate colonies join together to become the Australian nation?
Who can deliver a Welcome to Country?
options: Anyone that lives on the land.
An Aboriginal or Torres Strait Islander custodian of the land.
A Master of Ceremonies at an event on the land.
answers: An Aboriginal or Torres Strait Islander custodian of the land.

categories.section: Part 2 - Australia's democratic beliefs, rights and liberties

questions.question: Which is correct in Australian law?
options: Men and women have equal rights.
Men have more rights than women.
Women have more rights than men.
answers: Men and women have equal rights.

questions.question: Australians believe in freedom of speech. This means
options: people can say what they think about politics.
men have more legal rights than women.
everyone must follow a religion.
answers: people can say what they think about politics.

questions.question: In Australia, the government
options: tells people which religion to follow.
is separate from any religion.
makes laws based on the official religion.

questions.question: By law, Australian citizens aged 18 or over must
options: attend local council meetings.
vote in Australian elections.
join the Australian Defence Force.

questions.question: Which of the following is true?
options: Australian citizens can get an Australian passport.
Permanent residents can get an Australian passport.
Australian citizens need a visa to enter Australia.
answers: Australian citizens can get an Australian passport.

categories.section: Part 3 - Government and the law in Australia

questions.question: In Australian elections,
options: you are free and safe to vote for any candidate.
you must tell the police who you voted for.
you must write your name on your vote.
answers: you are free and safe to vote for any candidate.

questions.question: The Australian Constitution is a legal document that
options: contains religious rules.
contains rules of government.
can never be changed.

questions.question: In Australia, a referendum is a vote to change
options: the Australian Government.
the Australian Constitution.
the Prime Minister.

questions.question: In Australia, the parliament
options: makes and changes the laws.
is chosen by the Prime Minister.
is controlled by judges.

questions.question: The Governor-General represents
options: our head of state, the King of Australia.
a political party.
the current Prime Minister.
answers: our head of state, the King of Australia.

questions.question: Freedom of speech
options: underpins Australia’s democratic system.
is not an Australian value.
means people do not need to obey the law.

questions.question: Why is it important for people living in Australia to learn English?
options: Only native English speakers can become Australian citizens.
English is the only language spoken in Australian communities.
Speaking English helps people get an education and a job.
answers: Speaking English helps people get an education and a job.

questions.question: In Australia, the use of violence against a person is
options: acceptable if they are a different religion.
acceptable if they have a different opinion.
never acceptable and it is against the law.
answers: never acceptable and it is against the law.

questions.question: In Australia, we believe in mutual respect and tolerance. This means you can
options: physically fight someone when you disagree with them.
peacefully disagree with someone.
only agree with people from the same religion.

questions.question: In Australia, volunteering is important because
options: it strengthens our community.
it earns people lots of money.
we have to do it by law.
